source_title: Civilization #20: The Proto-Buddhists of the Indus Valley (Harappan) Civilization
summary: This December 2024 Indus Valley lecture is already-public Civilization As Inner Order support for trade, urban access, sanitation, peace, equality, and spiritual access as one non-palace, non-war social order, while adding bounded pressure for religious gatekeeping, climate/trade decline, and trade as moral comparison.

existing_lens_links.episode_phrase: trade machines, value-adding processing centers, customs systems, sewage systems, standardized brick worlds
existing_lens_links.rationale: The public episode read already links this phrase to the existing Civilization anchor because the active mechanism is the city's inner order: exchange, access, sanitation, standards, and shared urban life produce a different civilization form than palace, temple, or war.

existing_lens_links.episode_phrase: Buddhism's revolutionary line is that no Brahmin is needed to access Nirvana.
existing_lens_links.rationale: The existing anchor deliberately includes spiritual access without priestly monopoly as part of the IVC inheritance claim, while the page caveats Jiang's proto-Buddhist reconstruction as speculative.

concept_extensions.proposed_addition: Already public: keep this source as the Indus Valley countercase where trade, non-war urban form, customs walls, sanitation, standardization, peace, equality, and speculative spiritual inheritance form one non-palace, non-temple, non-war inner order.
concept_extensions.boundary_note: Civilization As Inner Order owns the source when the mechanism is an entire human arrangement: economy, city form, access pattern, peace, equality, and spiritual access becoming daily life. Do not split it into an Indus Valley topic page from this source alone.

concept_extensions.proposed_addition: Use as bounded future evidence only where Hindu/Brahmin hierarchy becomes an access-control mechanism: being good is not enough, Brahmins monopolize the route, kings sit beneath priests, Buddhism bypasses the gatekeeper, and caste appears as a counterattack.
concept_extensions.boundary_note: Religion As Administrative Filter owns the priestly access code. Civilization owns the broader IVC social order; Free Will owns agency if the contrast becomes obedience versus direct responsibility; Bureaucracy should not absorb this unless office, records, or institutional afterlife become the active mechanism.

concept_extensions.proposed_addition: Hold only bounded Strategy pressure from the contrast between trade-security arrangements and militarized city worlds: colonies, trusted partners, local security, and rare organized mass violence let long-distance trade move without turning the IVC itself into Mesopotamia.
concept_extensions.boundary_note: Strategy owns material security only when the question is how trade survives banditry, piracy, and organized violence. Civilization remains the primary home because the lecture's public mechanism is an inner order rather than a war plan.

concept_extensions.proposed_addition: Use only if a future trade-route compression needs the Bronze Age Gulf/Oxus/Afghanistan/tin/lapis layer: the IVC touches Egypt and Mesopotamia through route, partner, and material access rather than conquest.
concept_extensions.boundary_note: Chokepoint owns route/access density only if the route itself becomes the mechanism. It should not become a generic Bronze Age globalization or Indus page.

concept_extensions.proposed_addition: Keep as weak comparison pressure rather than a Sacred Machines extension: unlike cave, temple, pyramid, or ritual center materializing invisible order, this source's main public object is distributed city form and spiritual inheritance.
concept_extensions.boundary_note: Sacred Machines should not absorb this source unless later synthesis asks how material form bridges invisible order. The current public lens-point belongs to Civilization because the entire urban order is the mechanism.

new_lens_seeds.title: Trade As Moral Vantage
new_lens_seeds.core_mechanism: Long-distance trade can make a society witness neighboring worlds and define itself against their violence, hierarchy, waste, or sacred madness; exchange becomes a comparative moral education rather than only an economic network.
new_lens_seeds.reuse_potential: This could later compare IVC traders against other borderland or trade societies that learn by seeing adjacent orders, but current evidence is not yet broad enough for a public page.
new_lens_seeds.boundary_note: Hold this as pressure only. Civilization As Inner Order already carries the IVC application, while Borderland should receive it only if later sources show a repeatable edge/comparison mechanism beyond this one lecture.

chronology_notes.note: Dated 2024-12-03, this lecture is already the public Civilization As Inner Order layer for the IVC peak around 2600-1900 BCE and its trade-and-access countercase to Yamnaya property-war and later Bronze Age elite orders.

Jiang describes decline after the 4.2 kiloyear event as climate stress, trade collapse, urban depopulation, internal tension, migration, opportunistic violence, assimilation, and religious merger over roughly 300-500 years; preserve this as a dated source model, not a clean invasion story.

As of 2024-12-03, Jiang explicitly frames the IVC-as-proto-Buddhism continuity around false reality and oneness as speculation and says most scholars probably would not agree; public lens prose should preserve that caveat.

next_actions.action: No immediate public prose mutation is needed: Civilization As Inner Order already carries the source's public mechanism with lens-point:civilization-inner-order-trade-peace-access and the episode read already links exact marks to that anchor.

Do not create standalone Indus Valley Civilization, Harappan Civilization, Proto-Buddhists, Buddhism, Hinduism, Jainism, Sikhism, Brahmins, Caste System, Trade Civilization, Trade As Moral Vantage, Value-Adding Processing City, or Lost Trade Civilization Behind Buddhism pages from this source alone.

If public synthesis follows, prefer a Civilization As Inner Order replacement/compression only if several remaining Bronze Age gaps add pressure to trade-city, goddess/sky-god, collapse, or Greek-after-collapse chronology; otherwise keep this source as already-public support.

If provenance work follows, only repair exact links from this episode to lens-point:civilization-inner-order-trade-peace-access; avoid generic backlinks to Religion, Buddhism, Indus, or trade routes that blur Civilization, Administrative Filter, Strategy, Chokepoint, and Sacred Machines.
